spark.scene: True-color satellite view of the main Hawaiian Islands from the northwestern islands at upper left to the large island at lower right. Extensive white cumulus and layered clouds cover the southwestern ocean and cap the eastern side of the large island and parts of the smaller islands, with dark open ocean visible across the north and central-east. No distinct gray or brown haze, smoke or volcanic plume clearly separable from ordinary clouds is visible, with the southeastern part of the large island largely obscured by clouds.

classify.caveats: No plume found; nothing to classify.

kilauea.activity_summary: Kīlauea volcano is intermittently erupting short, precursory lava flows continuing the activity that began September 7. Summit inflation returned last night. Episode 55 fountaining is likely today, September 11, if inflation patterns remain consistent.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts increased in August, while the summit region showed no other signs of deformation. Mauna Loa had an increase in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 87 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the August reporting period, after 57 in July. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
